code: parsed_params = g_uri_parse_params ((const gchar *) data, (gssize) size, '&', FALSE);
note: Attacker-controlled input bytes (here "a=%", size 3) are passed directly as the params buffer and length to g_uri_parse_params.
end is set to params+3, bounding the parse region to the exact 3-byte input buffer.
For input "a=%", attr_end points at '=' (index 1), so attr length is 1 and value starts at index 2.

code: if (!uri_decode (&decoded_value, value, value_end - value, 0, G_URI_ERROR_MISC, NULL))
note: value points at the trailing '%' (index 2) and value_end-value is 1, so uri_decode is called on a 1-byte region ending at the buffer boundary.

code: for (s = start, end = s + length, d = decoded; s < end; s++)
note: Loop iterates over the single '%' byte; s points at the last byte of the 3-byte input buffer.
On seeing '%', the code reads s[1] and s[2] without checking that s+2 is within bounds; s[2] reads 1 byte past the end of the heap buffer, causing the heap-buffer-overflow READ.
